children: The engineering services company reports sequential growth across transportation, media and healthcare, while EBITDA margin improves to 21.9 per cent
Tata Elxsi reported revenue of Rs 1,055.7 crore in the second quarter of FY27, up 15 per cent from a year earlier and 3.4 per cent from the previous quarter.

The engineering and technology services company also reported an improvement in operating profitability. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 7.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 231.4 crore, while the EBITDA margin increased to 21.9 per cent from the previous quarter.
Growth came from all three of the company’s main businesses: transportation, media and communications, and healthcare and life sciences.
Tata Elxsi’s transportation business grew 2 per cent quarter-on-quarter in constant currency terms. The segment accounts for more than 55 per cent of its software development services business.

During the quarter, the company signed a multi-year contract with an automotive manufacturer to develop a cloud-based telematics and connected vehicle system. Such systems enable vehicles to exchange data and support connected services.
Tata Elxsi also partnered with Sarla Aviation to work on Shunya, an electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft.

The media and communications business grew 3.4 per cent sequentially in constant currency terms, supported by existing projects and new contracts. One of the new deals involves developing a generative artificial intelligence-based virtual assistant for a global technology company, with a focus on multilingual capabilities.

Healthcare and life sciences revenue grew 3.5 per cent quarter on quarter in constant currency terms. The company secured a product engineering contract from a global renal care company to redesign a home dialysis system. The work will cover product design, electronics, embedded systems and regulatory compliance.

Tata Elxsi also made an early-stage investment in Silicon Valley-based KAVIA AI in September. The investment builds on a partnership that began in July 2025 and focuses on using artificial intelligence to help businesses manage and modernise complex software systems.
